In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective method for degradation of two food dyes, namely E127 (erythrosine) and E132 (patent blue V), in aqueous solution by using the sonophotocatalysis.
a new photocatalytic degradation of two colorants food E127 and E132 in aqueous solutions.
the application of a sono-oxidation process for the removal of food dyes from aqueous solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sonochemical and photocatalytic processes are very effective for decoloration and mineralization of the food colorants studied.
the photocatalytic degradation of the two colorants is more effective than the sono-photocatalytic and the sono-catalytic processes.
the sonochemical and photocatalytic oxidation processes have been proved to be efficient and environmentally friendly processes for the degradation of two colorants E127 and E132.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sonochemical process ZnO/H2O2 is more effective than the sonochemical process, ZnO and UV ZnO.
the sono- and photo catalytic processes are effective in removing colorants from the aqueous phase, and the sono-catalytic process is more efficient than the photo catalytic process.
, in this study the degradation of food colorants E127 and E132 by sono-oxidation process using ZnO was investigated and compared with the degradation by UV, UV ZnO and UV ZnO H O2 processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photocatalytic degradation of the food dyes E132 and E127 was enhanced when H2O2 was added.
the sonocatalytic process using ZnO is more efficient for the degradation of E132 and E127.
the sono-photocatalytic process is a promising alternative for the degradation of dyes in aqueous media.
